a1.he: הָא בַּעַל מוּם שְׁרֵי, אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁלֹּא הִתִּירוּ מוּמְחֶה! תַּנָּא: כֹּל הֵיכָא דְּלֹא הִתִּירוֹ מוּמְחֶה — תָּם קָרֵי לֵיהּ.

a2.he: לֵימָא כְּתַנָּאֵי: הַתּוֹלֵשׁ צֶמֶר מִבְּכוֹר תָּם, אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁנּוֹלַד בּוֹ מוּם וּשְׁחָטוֹ — אָסוּר. בְּכוֹר בַּעַל מוּם שֶׁתָּלַשׁ מִמֶּנּוּ, וְאַחַר כָּךְ מֵת — עֲקַבְיָא בֶּן מַהֲלַלְאֵל מַתִּיר, וַחֲכָמִים אוֹסְרִים. אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה: לֹא בָּזֶה הִתִּיר עֲקַבְיָא בֶּן מַהֲלַלְאֵל, אֶלָּא בִּשְׂעַר בְּכוֹר בַּעַל מוּם שֶׁנָּשַׁר וְהִנִּיחוֹ בַּחַלּוֹן, וְאַחַר כָּךְ שְׁחָטוֹ — בָּזֶה עֲקַבְיָא בֶּן מַהֲלַלְאֵל מַתִּיר, וַחֲכָמִים אוֹסְרִין.

a3.he: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי: מוֹדֶה אַבָּא חֲלַפְתָּא בְּזֶה שֶׁהוּא מוּתָּר, אֲבָל בְּיִיחוּד אָמְרוּ חֲכָמִים: יַנִּיחֶנּוּ בַּחַלּוֹן, שֶׁמָּא יֵשׁ תִּקְוָה. שְׁחָטוֹ — דִּבְרֵי הַכֹּל מוּתָּר, מֵת — עֲקַבְיָא בֶּן מַהֲלַלְאֵל מַתִּיר וַחֲכָמִים אוֹסְרִים.

a4.he: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי — הַיְינוּ תַּנָּא קַמָּא! אֶלָּא לָאו הִתִּירוֹ מוּמְחֶה אִיכָּא בֵּינַיְיהוּ?

a5.he: דְּתַנָּא קַמָּא סָבַר: הִתִּירוֹ מוּמְחֶה — אִין, וְאִי לָא — לָא, וַאֲתָא רַבִּי יוֹסֵי לְמֵימַר: אַף עַל גַּב דְּלֹא הִתִּירוֹ מוּמְחֶה!

a6.he: אָמַר רָבָא: לָא, דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא אִי הִתִּירוֹ מוּמְחֶה — אִין, אִי לֹא הִתִּירוֹ — לָא, וְשָׁלֹשׁ מַחְלוֹקוֹת בַּדָּבָר, דְּתַנָּא קַמָּא סָבַר: פְּלִיגִי בְּמֵת, וְהוּא הַדִּין לִשְׁחָטוֹ, וְהַאי דְּקָמִיפַּלְגִי בְּמֵת — לְהוֹדִיעֲךָ כֹּחוֹ דַּעֲקַבְיָא.

a7.he: וְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה סָבַר: בְּמֵת — דִּבְרֵי הַכֹּל אָסוּר, כִּי פְּלִיגִי — בִּשְׁחָטוֹ, וַאֲתָא רַבִּי יוֹסֵי לְמֵימַר: בִּשְׁחָטוֹ — דִּבְרֵי הַכֹּל מוּתָּר, כִּי פְּלִיגִי — בְּמֵת.

a8.he: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן: הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה, הוֹאִיל וּתְנַן בִּבְחִירָתָא כְּוָותֵיהּ, דִּתְנַן: שְׂעַר בְּכוֹר בַּעַל מוּם שֶׁנָּשַׁר וְהִנִּיחוֹ בַּחַלּוֹן, וְאַחַר כָּךְ שְׁחָטוֹ — עֲקַבְיָא בֶּן מַהֲלַלְאֵל מַתִּיר, וַחֲכָמִים אוֹסְרִין.

a9.he: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק: מַתְנִיתִין נָמֵי דַּיְקָא, דִּתְנַן: צֶמֶר הַמְדוּלְדָּל בַּבְּכוֹר, אֶת שֶׁנִּרְאֶה עִם הַגִּיזָּה — מוּתָּר, וְאֶת שֶׁאֵינוֹ נִרְאֶה — אָסוּר.

a10.he: מַנִּי? אִילֵּימָא רַבִּי יוֹסֵי; וּבְמַאי? אִילֵימָא בִּשְׁחָטוֹ — בֵּין עֲקַבְיָא בֵּין רַבָּנַן, אִידֵּי וְאִידֵּי מִשְׁרָא שָׁרֵי!

a11.he: וְאֶלָּא בְּמֵת? וְאִי רַבָּנַן — אִידֵּי וְאִידֵּי מֵיסָר אָסְרִי, וְאִי עֲקַבְיָא — אִיפְּכָא מִיבַּעְיָא לֵיהּ: נִרְאֶה עִם הַגִּיזָּה — אָסוּר, דְּמִיתָה קָאָסְרָה לֵיהּ; אֵינוֹ נִרְאֶה עִם הַגִּיזָּה — מוּתָּר, דְּמֵעִיקָּרָא תְּלִישׁ!

a12.he: אֶלָּא פְּשִׁיטָא רַבִּי יְהוּדָה, וּבְמַאי? אִילֵימָא בְּמֵת — בֵּין לַעֲקַבְיָא בֵּין לְרַבָּנַן, אִידֵּי וְאִידֵּי מֵיסָר אָסְרִי!

a13.he: אֶלָּא לָאו בִּשְׁחָטוֹ? וְאִי עֲקַבְיָא — אִידֵּי וְאִידֵּי מִשְׁרָא שָׁרֵי! אֶלָּא לָאו רַבָּנַן הִיא? וּשְׁמַע מִינַּהּ: בִּשְׁחָטוֹ פְּלִיגִי. שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ.

a14.he: בָּעֵי רַבִּי יַנַּאי: הַתּוֹלֵשׁ צֶמֶר מֵעוֹלָה תְּמִימָה, מַהוּ? תּוֹלֵשׁ? מִי אִיכָּא מַאן דְּשָׁרֵי? אֶלָּא, צֶמֶר שֶׁנִּתְלַשׁ מֵעוֹלָה תְּמִימָה, מַהוּ?

a15.he: דְּחַטָּאת וְאָשָׁם לָא תִּיבְּעֵי לָךְ, דְּכֵיוָן דִּלְכַפָּרָה אָתוּ — לָא מְשַׁהוּ לְהוּ. דִּבְכוֹר וּמַעֲשֵׂר נָמֵי, דְּכֵיוָן דְּלָאו לְכַפָּרָה אָתוּ — מְשַׁהוּ לְהוּ. כִּי תִּיבְּעֵי לָךְ דְּעוֹלָה, מַאי? כֵּיוָן

b1.he: דְּעִיקַּר לָאו לְכַפָּרָה אָתֵי — מְשַׁהֵי לַהּ, אוֹ דִלְמָא, כֵּיוָן דְּעוֹלָה נָמֵי מְכַפְּרָא אַעֲשֵׂה — לָא מְשַׁהֵי לַהּ?

b2.he: תָּא שְׁמַע: הַתּוֹלֵשׁ צֶמֶר מִבְּכוֹר תָּם, אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁנּוֹלַד בּוֹ מוּם, שְׁחָטוֹ — אָסוּר. טַעְמָא דְּתוֹלֵשׁ, הָא נִתְלַשׁ — שָׁרֵי, וְכׇל שֶׁכֵּן עוֹלָה דְּלָא מְשַׁהֵי לַהּ!

b3.he: הוּא הַדִּין אֲפִילּוּ נִתְלַשׁ נָמֵי אָסוּר, וְהַאי דְּקָתָנֵי ״תּוֹלֵשׁ״ לְהוֹדִיעֲךָ כֹּחוֹ דַּעֲקַבְיָא, דִּבְבַעַל מוּם אֲפִילּוּ בְּתוֹלֵשׁ נָמֵי שָׁרֵי.

b4.he: וְהָאֲנַן ״נָשַׁר״ תְּנַן! תְּנָא ״נָשַׁר״ לְהוֹדִיעֲךָ כֹּחָן דְּרַבָּנַן, תְּנָא ״תּוֹלֵשׁ״ לְהוֹדִיעֲךָ כֹּחוֹ דַּעֲקַבְיָא.

b5.he: צֶמֶר הַמְדוּלְדָּל כּוּ׳. הֵיכִי דָּמֵי ״אֵינוֹ נִרְאֶה עִם הַגִּיזָּה״? אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר אָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ: כֹּל שֶׁעִיקָּרוֹ הָפוּךְ כְּלַפֵּי רֹאשׁוֹ. רַב נָתָן בַּר אוֹשַׁעְיָא אָמַר: כֹּל שֶׁאֵינוֹ מִתְמַעֵךְ עִם הַגִּיזָּה.

b6.he: וְרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ, מַאי טַעְמָא לָא אָמַר כְּרַב נָתָן בַּר אוֹשַׁעְיָא? אָמַר רַבִּי אִילְעָא: קָסָבַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ, לְפִי שֶׁאִי אֶפְשָׁר לַגִּיזָּה בְּלֹא נִימִין הַמְדוּלְדָּלוֹת.

b8.he: מַתְנִי׳ עַד כַּמָּה יִשְׂרָאֵל חַיָּיבִין לִיטַּפֵּל בִּבְכוֹר? בַּדַּקָּה — שְׁלֹשִׁים יוֹם, וּבַגַּסָּה — חֲמִשִּׁים יוֹם. רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר: בַּדַּקָּה — שְׁלֹשָׁה חֳדָשִׁים. אָמַר לוֹ הַכֹּהֵן בְּתוֹךְ הַזְּמַן: ״תְּנֵהוּ לִי״ — הֲרֵי זֶה לֹא יִתְּנֶנּוּ לוֹ. וְאִם בַּעַל מוּם הוּא, וְאָמַר לוֹ: ״תְּנֵהוּ לִי שֶׁאוֹכְלֶנּוּ״ — מוּתָּר. וּבִשְׁעַת הַמִּקְדָּשׁ, אִם הָיָה תָּמִים, אָמַר לוֹ: ״תֵּן [לִי] וְאַקְרִיבֶנּוּ״ — מוּתָּר.

b9.he: הַבְּכוֹר נֶאֱכָל שָׁנָה בְּשָׁנָה, בֵּין תָּם בֵּין בַּעַל מוּם, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״לִפְנֵי ה׳ אֱלֹהֶיךָ תֹאכְלֶנּוּ שָׁנָה בְשָׁנָה״. נוֹלַד לוֹ מוּם בְּתוֹךְ שְׁנָתוֹ — רַשַּׁאי לְקַיְּימוֹ כׇּל שְׁנֵים עָשָׂר חֹדֶשׁ. לְאַחַר שְׁנֵים עָשָׂר חֹדֶשׁ — אֵינוֹ רַשַּׁאי לְקַיְּימוֹ אֶלָּא שְׁלֹשִׁים יוֹם.

b10.he: גְּמָ׳ מְנָהָנֵי מִילֵּי? אָמַר רַב כָּהֲנָא: דְּאָמַר קְרָא ״בְּכוֹר בָּנֶיךָ תִּתֶּן לִּי״, ״כֵּן תַּעֲשֶׂה לְצֹאנֶךָ״.

b12.he: אֵיפוֹךְ אֲנָא! מִסְתַּבְּרָא דְּמַקְדַּם לְמַקְדַּם, דִּמְאַחַר לְדִמְאַחַר. אַדְּרַבָּה, דִּסְמִיךְ לֵיהּ לְדִסְמִיךְ לֵיהּ!

b13.he: אֶלָּא אָמַר רָבָא: אָמַר קְרָא ״תַּעֲשֶׂה״, הוֹסִיף לְךָ הַכָּתוּב עֲשִׂיָּיה אַחֶרֶת בְּשׁוֹרְךָ.

b14.he: וְאֵימָא: שִׁיתִּין! לֹא מְסָרְךָ הַכָּתוּב אֶלָּא לַחֲכָמִים.

b15.he: תַּנְיָא נָמֵי הָכִי: ״בְּכוֹר בָּנֶיךָ תִּתֶּן לִי״, ״כֵּן תַּעֲשֶׂה לְצֹאנֶךָ״ — יָכוֹל אַף לְשׁוֹרְךָ? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: ״תַּעֲשֶׂה״ — הוֹסִיף לְךָ הַכָּתוּב עֲשִׂיָּיה אַחֶרֶת בְּשׁוֹרְךָ, לֹא מְסָרְךָ הַכָּתוּב אֶלָּא לַחֲכָמִים.

b16.he: מִכָּאן אָמְרוּ: עַד כַּמָּה יִשְׂרָאֵל חַיָּיבִין לְהִטַּפֵּל בִּבְכוֹר? בִּבְהֵמָה דַּקָּה — שְׁלֹשִׁים יוֹם, בְּגַסָּה — חֲמִשִּׁים יוֹם. רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר: בַּדַּקָּה — שְׁלֹשָׁה חֳדָשִׁים, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁטִּפּוּלָהּ מְרוּבָּה. תָּנָא: מִפְּנֵי שֶׁשִּׁינֶּיהָ דַּקּוֹת.

b17.he: אִם אָמַר לוֹ הַכֹּהֵן בְּתוֹךְ הַזְּמַן ״תְּנֵהוּ לִי״, הֲרֵי זֶה לֹא יִתֵּן לוֹ. מַאי טַעְמָא? אָמַר רַב שֵׁשֶׁת: מִפְּנֵי שֶׁנִּרְאֶה כְּכֹהֵן הַמְסַיֵּיעַ בְּבֵית הַגֳּרָנוֹת.

b18.he: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: הַכֹּהֲנִים וְהַלְוִיִּם וְהָעֲנִיִּים הַמְסַיְּיעִים בְּבֵית הָרוֹעִים, וּבְבֵית הַגֳּרָנוֹת, וּבְבֵית הַמִּטְבָּחַיִם — אֵין נוֹתְנִין לָהֶם תְּרוּמָה וּמַעֲשֵׂר בִּשְׂכָרָן, וְאִם עוֹשִׂין כֵּן חִילֵּלוּ, וַעֲלֵיהֶן הַכָּתוּב אוֹמֵר: ״שִׁחַתֶּם בְּרִית הַלֵּוִי״, וְאוֹמֵר: ״וְאֶת קׇדְשֵׁי בְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל לֹא תְחַלְּלוּ וְלֹא תָמוּתוּ״.

b19.he: מַאי ״וְאוֹמֵר״? וְכִי תֵּימָא: מִיתָה לָא — תָּא שְׁמַע: ״וְאֶת קׇדְשֵׁי בְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל לֹא תְחַלְּלוּ וְלֹא תָמוּתוּ״.

b20.he: וּבִקְּשׁוּ חֲכָמִים לְקוֹנְסָן, וְלִהְיוֹת מַפְרִישִׁין עֲלֵיהֶן תְּרוּמָה מִשָּׁלֵם, וּמִפְּנֵי מָה לֹא קְנָסוּם? דִּלְמָא אָתֵי לְאַפְרוֹשֵׁי מִן הַפְּטוּר עַל הַחִיּוּב.

messages.text: Continued from 25b: Rabbi Asi said in the name of Reish Lakish that Akavya ben Mahalalel and the Rabbis disagree about the shed wool of a blemished firstborn only where an expert had already deemed the animal permitted for slaughter; otherwise all agree it is prohibited. The Gemara raised an objection from a baraita: one who plucks the wool of an unblemished firstborn may not use it, even if it later developed a blemish and was slaughtered. The reason is that it was unblemished…
…But in the case of a blemished firstborn, use of its wool is permitted, even though an expert did not deem the animal permitted for slaughter. This contradicts the statement of Rabbi Asi.

notes.he: ור' יוסי הוא דאמר בשחטו שרו רבנן אי נמי עקביא היא אע"ג דלא התירו וקשיא לריש לקיש:
notes.en: But a blemished one is permitted: and it is Rabbi Yosei, who said that where he slaughtered it the Rabbis permit [the wool]; or else it is Akavya, [who permits it] even though [an expert] did not deem it permitted. And this is difficult for Reish Lakish.

notes.he: תולש לכ"ש נושר:
notes.en: But a blemished one is permitted: [if this is so where one] plucked, all the more so [where the wool] shed.

notes.he: קודם אלא לאחר שנשר:
notes.en: And even though an expert did not deem it permitted: beforehand, but only after it shed.

messages.text: It is possible that the tanna of that baraita calls the animal unblemished wherever an expert did not yet deem the firstborn permitted for slaughter, even if it was physically blemished.

notes.he: ומאי אע"פ שנולד בו מום אע"פ שנראה אחר כן לחכם ואמר מום קבוע:
notes.en: It calls it unblemished: and what does “even though a blemish developed in it” mean? Even though it was afterward shown to a Sage and he said it is a permanent blemish.

notes.he: א"ל ריש לקיש האי תנא דהתולש צמר כל היכא דלא התירו מומחה קודם שתלש תם קרי ליה שכתולש מתם דמי וליכא למימר הא בעל מום שרי (על שנטמא היינו שהומם):
notes.en: Reish Lakish said to him: this tanna of “one who plucks wool” calls it unblemished wherever an expert did not deem it permitted before he plucked, for it is like plucking from an unblemished one; so one cannot say, “but a blemished one is permitted.” [Rabbeinu Gershom puts this answer in Reish Lakish’s mouth; the daf gives it in the Gemara’s voice.] (The printed text adds: “that became impure,” that is, that became blemished.)

messages.text: Let us say that the interpretation of Reish Lakish is the subject of a dispute between tanna’im, as the baraita states:

notes.he: הא דר"ל תנאי היא:
notes.en: Let us say: that this [statement] of Reish Lakish is the subject of a dispute between tanna’im.

messages.text: With regard to one who plucks the wool from an unblemished firstborn, even though it later developed a blemish and the owner slaughtered it, use of the wool is prohibited.

notes.he: דבתם אפילו עקביא מודה דאתו לשהוייה ולאפקועי מקדושת מזבח ועוד שהרי עדיין אין בו שום היתר. אע"ג דנקט תולש הוא הדין לנתלש כדמפרש בסיפא דשמעתא:
notes.en: Prohibited: for with an unblemished one even Akavya concedes, since people would come to keep it [alive] and to strip it of its sanctity for the altar; moreover, it does not yet have any permission at all. And although it uses [the word] “plucks,” the same applies to [wool] that was torn out [by itself], as is explained at the end of the discussion.

messages.text: In the case of a blemished firstborn from which one plucked wool, and it subsequently died, Akavya ben Mahalalel deems the wool permitted and the Rabbis deem it prohibited.

notes.he: הכא לא קתני והניחו בחלון משום דרשע הוא שתולש ודעתו ליהנות לאלתר אבל בנשר קתני והניחו בחלון:
notes.en: A blemished firstborn from which one plucked: here it does not teach “and placed it in a compartment,” because one who plucks is wicked and intends to benefit at once; but where it shed, it does teach “and placed it in a compartment.”

messages.text: It was not with regard to that case that Akavya ben Mahalalel deemed use of the wool permitted.

notes.he: שמת התיר עקביא אלא בשחטו:
notes.en: Not in this: [the case] where it died, did Akavya permit, but where he slaughtered it.

messages.text: Rather, it was in a case of the hair of a blemished firstborn animal that shed from the animal and one placed the hair in a compartment, and thereafter one slaughtered the animal. In that case Akavya ben Mahalalel deems use of the wool permitted, and the Rabbis deem its use prohibited.
My father, Ḥalafta, concedes to Akavya ben Mahalalel in this case of a slaughtered firstborn that use of the wool is permitted.

notes.he: ששמו חלפתא שהוא מן החכמים החולקין על עקביא ומודה הוא בזה ששחטו שהוא מותר:
notes.en: Rabbi Yosei said: My father concedes: whose name was Ḥalafta, who is one of the Sages who disagree with Akavya, and he concedes in this [case], where he slaughtered it, that it is permitted.

notes.he: מודה אבא חלפתא בזה ששחטו שהוא מותר אפילו לחכמים:
notes.en: My father Ḥalafta concedes in this [case], where he slaughtered it, that it is permitted, even according to the Sages.

messages.text: Indeed [aval], the Rabbis said explicitly: One places it in a compartment, as perhaps there is a hope that use of the wool will ultimately be permitted, since if he slaughters the animal all agree that use of the wool is permitted.

notes.he: שבאמת ובברור אמרו יניחנו בחלון לשער בכור בעל מום שנשר:
notes.en: But be’yiḥud the Sages said: that truly and clearly the Sages said one should place the hair of a blemished firstborn that shed in a compartment.

notes.he: באמת וחבירו בעירובין בפרק בכל מערבין (עירובין דף לח.) בסופו:
notes.en: Aval: [means] truly; and a parallel to it is in Eruvin, in the chapter Bakol Me’arvin (Eruvin 38a), at its end.

notes.he: בברור וחבירו במסכת יומא (דף נד.) וידעו בייחוד ששם ארון נגנז:
notes.en: Be’yiḥud: clearly; and a parallel to it is in tractate Yoma (54a): “And they knew be’yiḥud that the Ark was hidden there.”

notes.he: שמא יהא מותר ליהנות. ומפרש ומה תקוה יש שאם שחטו דברי הכל מותר:
notes.en: Perhaps there is hope: perhaps it will become permitted to derive benefit [from it]. And he explains what hope there is: that if he slaughters it, all agree it is permitted.

notes.he: האי אבל כמו באמת כדכתיב אבל אשמים אנחנו. בייחוד בבירור:
notes.en: But be’yiḥud they said: this aval is like “truly,” as it is written: “Aval we are guilty” (Genesis 42:21). Be’yiḥud: clearly.

notes.he: ונותנו בחלון שיש לו תקנה שאם שחטו יהא מותר:
notes.en: And he places it in a compartment, for it has a remedy: if he slaughters it, it will be permitted.

messages.text: But if the animal dies by other means, Akavya ben Mahalalel deems use of the wool permitted and the Rabbis deem it prohibited.

If that is the explanation of their dispute, the opinion of Rabbi Yosei is identical to the opinion of the first tanna in the baraita, as both hold that use of the wool of a slaughtered blemished firstborn is permitted and the dispute between Akavya ben Mahalalel and the Rabbis applies to a case where the animal dies by other means.
messages.quote: concedes to Akavya ben Mahalalel in this case of a slaughtered firstborn

notes.he: דקאמר התולש צמר מבכור תם ושחטו אסור הא בעל מום ושחטו מותר לדברי הכל ובמת פליגי במודה דר' יוסי ולת"ק נמי במת פליגי:
notes.en: Rabbi Yosei is the same as the first tanna: who said, “One who plucks wool from an unblemished firstborn and slaughtered it, it is prohibited”; by inference, [wool plucked from] a blemished one that he slaughtered is permitted according to all, and they disagree where it died. In Rabbi Yosei’s “concedes” too they disagree where it died, and according to the first tanna as well they disagree where it died.

notes.he: ר' יוסי דאמר במת נחלקו היינו ת"ק דאמר דבמת חולקין:
notes.en: On what did they disagree etc.: Rabbi Yosei, who said they disagreed where it died, is the same as the first tanna, who said they disagree where it died.

messages.text: Rather, is it not correct to say the dispute between them concerns the requirement that an expert deem the animal permitted for slaughter?

As the first tanna holds: If an expert deemed the animal permitted before its wool was shed, then yes, use of the wool is permitted after the animal has been slaughtered; but if not, then use of the wool is not permitted.

notes.dh: תנא קמא סבר אי התירו מומחה אין אי לא לא
notes.he: דבעל כרחיך הכי תרצת וכדתרצת ריש לקיש לעיל כי אותביניה מרישא דמילתיה דתנא קמא דקתני התולש צמר מבכור תם הא בעל מום שרי ותרצה ריש לקיש ואמר כל היכא דלא התיר מומחה תם קרי ליה אלמא הכי משמע מילתיה התולש צמר מבכור תם דהיינו בעל מום שלא התירו מומחה אסור לדברי הכל הא בכור בעל מום דהיינו התירו מומחה שתלש ממנו כו' ור' יוסי סבר אע"ג דלא התירו מומחה נמי כשנשר שרו רבנן ממאי מדקאמר יש תקוה דמשמע יש תקוה ויתירנו מומחה וישחטנו מכלל דאכתי לא התירו מומחה כשנשר:
notes.en: The first tanna holds: if an expert deemed it permitted, yes; if not, no: for you must explain it this way, just as you explained it for Reish Lakish above, when we raised an objection to him from the first clause of the first tanna’s words, which teaches “one who plucks wool from an unblemished firstborn,” implying that a blemished one is permitted, and Reish Lakish answered: wherever an expert did not deem it permitted, he calls it unblemished. Evidently this is the meaning of his words: one who plucks wool from an unblemished firstborn, that is, a blemished one that an expert did not deem permitted, it is prohibited according to all; but a blemished firstborn, that is, one an expert deemed permitted, from which one plucked etc. And Rabbi Yosei holds that even though an expert did not deem it permitted when it shed, the Rabbis permit it. From where [do we know this]? From his saying “there is hope,” which implies there is hope that an expert will deem it permitted and he will slaughter it; by inference, an expert had not yet deemed it permitted when it shed. [Rashi, like Rabbeinu Gershom, attributes the earlier answer to Reish Lakish; the daf gives it in the Gemara’s voice.]

notes.dh: דתנא קמא סבר אי התירו אין אי לא לא
notes.he: פירש בקונטרס דכיון דתריצנא לעיל דכל היכא דלא התירו מומחה תם קרי ליה אם כן סיפא דקרי ליה בעל מום מיירי בלא התרת מומחה וקשיא לפירושו דהא דתירץ הכי לעיל היינו כי היכי דאיתוקם לריש לקיש ככולי עלמא אבל השתא דצרכינן לומר ממה נפשך כתנאי מסתברא לומר איפכא דתהוי מילתיה כתנא קמא כפשטיה ונראה לפרש דסובר הש"ס עכשיו משום דקאמר ר' יוסי שמא יש תקוה שעל סמך השחיטה לא היה אומר כך שזה בידו ואין כאן שמא אבל בהתרת מומחה קאמר שמא יש תקוה שיזדקק לו חכם להתירו ואין זה כל כך דבר ברור דמי יימר דמזדקק ליה מומחה ומ"מ במסקנא קאמר שמא יש תקוה דקמיירי בשחיטה:
notes.en: For the first tanna holds: if an expert deemed it permitted, yes; if not, no: The Kuntres [Rashi] explained that since we answered above that wherever an expert did not deem it permitted he calls it unblemished, the latter clause, which calls it blemished, speaks of [an animal] an expert deemed permitted. But this is difficult for his explanation: the reason [the Gemara] answered so above was in order to establish Reish Lakish according to everyone; but now that we must say, in either case, that it is a dispute of tanna’im, it is more reasonable to say the reverse, so that the words of the first tanna stand according to their plain meaning. It seems [better] to explain that the Talmud now holds so because Rabbi Yosei says “perhaps there is hope”: he would not have said this with reference to slaughter, which is in the owner’s own hands, so there is no “perhaps” about it; rather, he says “perhaps there is hope” with reference to an expert’s permission, that a Sage may attend to him and deem it permitted, and that is not so certain a thing, for who says an expert will attend to him? Nevertheless, in the conclusion [the Gemara] says “perhaps there is hope” refers to slaughter.

messages.text: And Rabbi Yosei comes to say that even in a case where an expert did not deem the firstborn permitted for slaughter before its wool was shed, use of the wool is still permitted. If so, the interpretation of Reish Lakish is the subject of the dispute between the first tanna and Rabbi Yosei: The first tanna agrees with that opinion and Rabbi Yosei rejects it.

notes.he: מה שעקביא מתיר במת כשהתירו מומחה קודם תלישת שער ואתא ר' יוסי למימר דכל תנא בתרא מטפי אע"ג דלא התירו מומחה קודם אלא שוב [אחר תלישה] מתיר עקביא והיינו כתנאי:
notes.en: The first tanna holds: what Akavya permits where it died is [only] where an expert deemed it permitted before the hair was plucked. And Rabbi Yosei comes to say, for every later tanna adds something, that even though an expert did not deem it permitted beforehand but only afterward [after it was plucked], Akavya permits it. And so it is a dispute of tanna’im.

messages.text: No, the interpretation of Reish Lakish is not the subject of their dispute, as everyone agrees that if an expert deemed the animal permitted before its wool was shed, then yes, use of the wool is permitted, but if an expert did not deem the animal permitted beforehand then the use of its wool is not permitted.
messages.quote: the dispute between them concerns the requirement that an expert deem the animal permitted

notes.dh: לא דכולי עלמא אי התירו מומחה
notes.he: קודם תלישה אין אי לא לא ולאו בהכי פליגי אלא ג' מחלוקת בדבר:
notes.en: No, everyone agrees that if an expert deemed it permitted: before the plucking, yes; if not, no; and they do not disagree about this. Rather, there are three disputes in the matter.

messages.text: And there are three disputes concerning this matter, as the first tanna holds: Akavya ben Mahalalel and the Rabbis disagree with regard to a case where the firstborn died, and the same is true, i.e., they disagree, in a case where he slaughtered it.

notes.he: מדלא אשכחן במילתיה דתנא קמא דנימא שחטו דברי הכל מותר:
notes.en: They disagree where it died, and the same applies where he slaughtered it: since we do not find in the words of the first tanna that he says that where he slaughtered it all agree it is permitted.

notes.dh: דת"ק סבר פליגי במת וה"ה לשחטו
notes.he: ומשום דלא איירי מידי בשחטו אית לן למימר דסבר דבתרווייהו פליגי:
notes.en: For the first tanna holds that they disagree where it died, and the same is true where he slaughtered it: since he said nothing about [a case] where he slaughtered it, we must say that he holds they disagree in both.

messages.text: And the reason that the first tanna states they disagree specifically in a case where it died is to convey to you the far-reaching nature of the opinion of Akavya, i.e., that he deems use of the wool permitted even if the animal was not slaughtered.

And Rabbi Yehuda holds: With regard to a firstborn that died, all, i.e., Akavya ben Mahalalel and the Rabbis, agree that use of the wool is prohibited, and when they disagree it is with regard to a case where the owner slaughtered the animal.
And Rabbi Yosei comes to say: Where he slaughtered it, all agree that use of the wool is permitted, and when they disagree it is with regard to a case where the animal died.

messages.caption: Rava’s three disputes over the shed wool of a blemished firstborn: where Akavya ben Mahalalel and the Rabbis disagree, according to each reading.

messages.text: The halakha is in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Yehuda, since we learned a mishna in our preferred tractate in accordance with his opinion. As we learned in a mishna (Eduyyot 5:6):

notes.he: דבשחטו פליגי ולא במת:
notes.en: The halakha is in accordance with Rabbi Yehuda: that they disagree where he slaughtered it, and not where it died.

notes.he: דלא שרי עקביא אלא בשחטו:
notes.en: The halakha is in accordance with Rabbi Yehuda: that Akavya permits only where he slaughtered it.

notes.he: מסכת עדיות:
notes.en: Bivḥirta [in our preferred tractate]: tractate Eduyot.

messages.text: In the case of the hair of a blemished firstborn animal that shed from the animal and one placed the hair in a compartment, and thereafter he slaughtered the animal, Akavya ben Mahalalel deems use of the wool permitted and the Rabbis deem its use prohibited even after the animal’s death.
The mishna is also precisely formulated so that this conclusion can be inferred, as we learned in the latter clause of the mishna:

With regard to wool that was not completely shed which is dangling from a firstborn animal, that which appears to be part of the fleece is permitted when the animal is shorn after its death, and that which does not appear to be part of the fleece is prohibited.

notes.he: המדולדל:
notes.en: Wool that is medublal: [that is,] medouldal, dangling.

notes.he: שנראה במחובר לגיזה מותר:
notes.en: That appears with the fleece: what appears attached to the fleece is permitted.

messages.text: In accordance with whose opinion is this ruling? If we say it is in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Yosei, that is difficult: But in what case did he issue this ruling?
messages.quote: that which appears to be part of the fleece is permitted

messages.text: If we say it was in a case where he slaughtered it that cannot be correct, as whether the halakha follows the opinion of Akavya or whether it follows the opinion of the Rabbis, in both this case of wool that appears to be part of the fleece and that case where it does not, the use of the wool is permitted.

notes.he: בין נראה בין לא נראה מישרי שרי דהא אפי' מונח בחלון קא"ר יוסי דאפי' רבנן שרו בשחטו:
notes.en: This and that: whether it appears or does not appear, it is permitted, for Rabbi Yosei said that even [wool] placed in a compartment the Rabbis too permit where he slaughtered it.

notes.he: בין נראה ובין שאינו נראה כדאמרינן דבשחטו דברי הכל מותר:
notes.en: This and that: whether it appears or does not appear [with the fleece], as we said that where he slaughtered it, all agree it is permitted.

messages.text: Rather, if one says this is referring to a case where the animal died, that too is difficult. But that cannot be correct either, since if the halakha is in accordance with the Rabbis, then both this wool and that wool are prohibited.

notes.dh: אי רבנן אידי ואידי מיסר אסרי
notes.he: דאותו שמחובר בו טעון קבורה לדברי הכל והתלוש ממנו רבנן אסרי ליה אפי' מונח בחלון:
notes.en: If the Rabbis, both this and that are prohibited: for what is attached to it requires burial according to all, and what is detached from it the Rabbis prohibit, even [wool] placed in a compartment.

notes.dh: אי רבנן אידי ואידי מיסר אסירי
notes.he: אפילו אותן שנתלש קודם וכ"ש ששוב נתלש שמיתה אוסרת:
notes.en: If the Rabbis, both this and that are prohibited: even [the hairs] that were plucked earlier, and all the more so what was plucked afterward, since death renders it prohibited.

messages.text: And if the halakha is in accordance with Akavya, then the mishna should have stated the opposite ruling: If the dangling wool appears to be part of the fleece it is prohibited, as the death of the animal renders it prohibited because it is considered attached to the animal; if it does not appear to be part of the fleece it is permitted, as it was considered detached from the beginning, before the animal died.

notes.he: שמה שהוא מותר במת אין מתיר אלא מה שנושר קודם אבל [מה שנושר] שוב [אחר] שמת [לדברי] הכל אסור והכי איבעי ליה למיתנא את שאינו נראה מותר ואת שנראה אסור:
notes.en: And if Akavya, it should be the reverse: for when he permits where it died, he permits only what shed beforehand, but what shed after it died is prohibited according to all. So it should have taught: what does not appear is permitted, and what appears is prohibited.

messages.text: Rather, it is obvious that this clause of the mishna is in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Yehuda.

notes.he: דאמר בשחטו פליגי:
notes.en: Rather, it is obvious that it is Rabbi Yehuda: who said they disagree where he slaughtered it.

messages.text: And in what case does the mishna’s ruling apply? If we say it is referring to a case where the animal died, then whether the halakha is in accordance with the opinion of Akavya or whether it is in accordance with the opinion of the Rabbis, in both this case of wool that appears to be part of the fleece and that case where it does not, the use of the wool is prohibited.

notes.he: בין נראה בין לא נראה:
notes.en: This and that: whether it appears or does not appear.

messages.text: Rather, is it not referring to a case where he slaughtered the animal? And consequently, if the mishna is in accordance with the opinion of Akavya, then in both this case of wool that appears to be part of the fleece and that case where it does not, use of the wool is permitted.

Rather, is it not correct to say the mishna is in accordance with the opinion of the Rabbis? And accordingly, one may conclude from it that Akavya and the Rabbis disagree in a case where he slaughtered the animal?

notes.he: מדלא מצית מוקמת ליה בגוונא אחריתי ומדסתם לן כר' יהודה ש"מ הלכתא כוותיה:
notes.en: And conclude from it that they disagree where he slaughtered it: since you cannot establish it in any other way. And since [the mishna] taught us anonymously in accordance with Rabbi Yehuda, conclude from it that the halakha is in accordance with him.

notes.he: דבשחטו אוסרין מה שקודם נשר אבל שוב שנשחט מותר העור והמחובר לו והיינו דקאמר הנראה עם הגיזה הצמר המחובר לעור קרי גיזה מותר ואת שאינו נראה אסור:
notes.en: Rather, is it not the Rabbis: who, where he slaughtered it, prohibit what shed beforehand; but after it was slaughtered, the hide and what is attached to it are permitted. And that is what it says: what appears with the fleece is permitted, for it calls the wool attached to the hide “fleece”; and what does not appear is prohibited.

messages.text: Indeed, conclude from it that this is so.
messages.quote: conclude from it that Akavya and the Rabbis disagree in a case where he slaughtered the animal

messages.caption: Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak’s proof: of the four ways to read the dangling-wool mishna, only the Rabbis as Rabbi Yehuda reports them, where the animal was slaughtered, fit it.

messages.text: With regard to one who plucks wool from an unblemished burnt offering which was later slaughtered, what is the halakha?

notes.he: מחיים לרבנן מהו לאחר שחיטת בעלת מום לא תיבעי לך דוודאי לרבנן אסור דאי שרית ליה אתי לשהוייה ואתי לידי גיזה ועבודה:
notes.en: One who plucks wool from an unblemished burnt offering: [plucked] during its life; according to the Rabbis, what is [the halakha]? About [wool of] a blemished one, after slaughter, you need not ask, for according to the Rabbis it is certainly prohibited: if you permit it, one will come to keep it [alive] and come to [violate the prohibitions of] shearing and labor.

notes.he: יש פירוש מרש"י שכתוב בהם שהוממה ואח"כ נפדית ושחטה משמע שהעמידה כן כדי שתהא כעין בכור אלא שהתלישה היתה בתמות ותימה והא בעי האי צמר העמדה והערכה ואין מועיל לצמר העמדת הבהמה כדמוכח בפ' ראשית הגז (חולין קלה.) גבי הא דקאמר התם דאין ראשית הגז נוהג בקדשים משום דכתיב צאנך ולא של הקדש ומוקי לה למעוטי קדשי בדק הבית ופריך והא בעי העמדה והערכה וי"ל דסבירא ליה כר"ל דאית ליה בפ"ב דתמורה (דף לב:) לרבנן דקדשי מזבח לא היו בכלל העמדה והערכה והכי נמי אשכחן רב דסבר כוותיה בפ' שני (לעיל בכורות טו.) ועוד י"ל דקדשי מזבח שיש עליהם קדושת הגוף בטל הצמר אגב הבהמה אפילו אותו שנתלש ובר העמדה והערכה חשיב ולא דמי לקדשי בדק הבית א"נ חשיב האי צמר כבעל מום מעיקרא וכן שופר של עולה לא יתקע ואם תקע יצא משום דכיון דמעל נפק לחולין כדקאמר בפרק ראוהו ב"ד (ר"ה כח.) משמע דשייך ביה פדיון ועוד יש לפרש שופר של עולה שהוקדשה הבהמה לדמי עולה ושופר שלמים שהוקדשה הבהמה לדמי שלמים ודינה כשלמים עצמן ואין בה מעילה כדקאמר בפ"ב דפסחים (דף כז:) בעצי שלמים עסקינן ומיהו קשה בהך דשמעתין דכיון דבעי הצמר פדיון היכי שייך למיגזר דלמא משהי ליה והא צריך לפדותו דמה היה מרויח וקצת היה נראה לפרש דאיירי בעולה ונשחטה למזבח שזריקת הדם מתרת בשרה למזבח והעור לכהנים ומבעיא ליה בצמר שנתלש אי משתרי נמי בהכי אבל פלוגתא דאמוראי היא בפרק המזבח מקדש (זבחים פו.) בעצמות שפרשו לפני זריקה דרבי זירא סבר דזריקה מתירתן אפילו לקתא דנרגי וחציני וקאמר התם כרבי אלעזר דאמר רבי אלעזר פרשו לפני זריקה מועלין בהם ופירש שם בקונטרס דמועלין לעולם אף לאחר זריקה וכל שכן דאינה מתרת מה שפירש מחיים ומיהו יש ספרים דגרסי התם כרבי אלעזר דאמר ר' אלעזר פרשו לפני זריקה מועלין בהן עד זריקה כו:
notes.en: In brief: One version of Rashi’s commentary reads [the case as one where the burnt offering] “became blemished, was afterward redeemed, and he slaughtered it,” to make it resemble a firstborn, with the plucking done while it was unblemished. Tosafot ask: such wool would itself need to be stood and valuated [before redemption], and standing the animal does not help for the wool, as is evident in Reshit HaGez (Ḥullin 135a). They answer: (1) he holds like Reish Lakish, who says in the second chapter of Temura (32b) that according to the Rabbis altar offerings were not included in standing and valuation, and Rav holds the same in chapter two (above, Bekhorot 15a); (2) with altar offerings, which have inherent sanctity, the wool is subordinate to the animal, even what was plucked, unlike consecrated property for Temple maintenance; or (3) this wool is regarded as if from a blemished animal from the outset. They compare the shofar of a burnt offering, with which one fulfills the obligation because it becomes non-sacred through misuse (Rosh HaShana 28a), or which is explained as an animal consecrated for its value (compare Pesaḥim 27b). Still, Tosafot ask: if the wool needs redemption anyway, what would the owner gain by keeping the animal, so why decree? They suggest instead that the case is a burnt offering slaughtered for the altar, whose blood sprinkling permits the hide to the priests, and the question is whether wool torn out [during its life] is also permitted by it. But this depends on a dispute of amora’im in HaMizbe’aḥ Mekadesh (Zevaḥim 86a) on bones that separated before sprinkling: Rabbi Zeira holds sprinkling permits them, while Rabbi Elazar holds one is liable for misusing them, which Rashi there explains as forever; though some texts there read “until sprinkling.” Open on Sefaria for the full text.

notes.he: מבעל מום דשאר קדשים לא קא מיבעי ליה כיון דבר פדייה הוא לא משהי ליה אלא פריק ליה ושחיט ליה מיד הלכך שרי. וא"ד (ה"מ) [כיון דבעי] מומחה ודאי איכא למיחש דמשהי להו ולא קא מיבעי ליה. אלא תמימה קא מיבעי ליה:
notes.en: From an unblemished burnt offering: about a blemished one of other consecrated animals he does not ask, since it can be redeemed one does not keep it, but redeems it and slaughters it at once; therefore it is permitted. And some say: since it requires an expert, there is certainly concern that one will keep them, and he does not ask. Rather, he asks about an unblemished one.

messages.text: If one intentionally violates a prohibition and plucks the wool from an unblemished consecrated animal, is there anyone who deems it permitted? All agree that use of the wool is prohibited in such a case.
messages.quote: one who plucks wool from an unblemished burnt offering

notes.he: אליבא דרבנן הא וודאי רשע הוא:
notes.en: Is there anyone who permits it: according to the Rabbis? This one is certainly a wicked person.

notes.he: פירש בקונטרס אליבא דרבנן הא וודאי רשע הוא משמע דלעקביא אפשר דמותר אף על פי שהאמת הוא דלעקביא נמי אסור בתם כדמוכח ברייתא דהתולש צמר מבכור תם מכל מקום פירש כך בקונטרס שאפילו לא שמיעא ליה ברייתא דבר פשוט הוא דמיהא לרבנן דתולש אסור:
notes.en: Plucks: is there anyone who permits it? The Kuntres [Rashi] explained: according to the Rabbis, this one is certainly a wicked person. This implies that according to Akavya it might be permitted, although in truth, according to Akavya too it is prohibited with an unblemished animal, as is evident from the baraita “one who plucks wool from an unblemished firstborn.” Nevertheless the Kuntres explained it so because, even without that baraita, it is a simple matter that according to the Rabbis, at least, [wool one] plucked is prohibited.

messages.text: Rather, Rabbi Yannai’s question was: With regard to wool that was torn out by itself from an unblemished burnt offering, what is the halakha?

Do not raise the dilemma concerning the wool of a sin offering and a guilt offering. Since these offerings come for atonement the owner does not keep them longer than necessary, and therefore there is no reason to deem the wool prohibited.

notes.he: מעצמו דחטאת ואשם וכו' דבכור ומעשר נמי לא תיבעי לך לד"ה אסור דלאו לכפרה אתי ומשהי ליה משום חימוד צמר הנושר ואתי לידי תקלה:
notes.en: Wool that was torn out: by itself. Of a sin offering and a guilt offering etc.; of a firstborn and tithe, too, you need not ask: according to all it is prohibited, since they do not come for atonement, and one keeps them out of desire for the wool that sheds, and comes to a stumbling.

messages.text: Likewise, with regard to the wool of a firstborn and an animal tithe offering there is also no dilemma. Since they do not come for atonement one might keep them longer than necessary, and therefore the wool is prohibited in order to prevent one from violating the prohibition against shearing the animal or using it for labor.
Rather, when you raise the dilemma, it is with regard to the wool of a burnt offering. What is the halakha? Does one say that since…

notes.he: כיון דלאו לכפרה אתיא דדורון בעלמא היא משהי לה:
notes.en: When you raise the dilemma, it is about a burnt offering: since it does not come for atonement, for it is merely a gift, one keeps it.

messages.text: …being brought for atonement is not its primary function, there is a concern that one might keep it? Or perhaps, since a burnt offering also effects atonement for neglecting to perform a positive mitzva, one does not keep the animal longer than necessary.

notes.he: דאינו מביאה על חטא:
notes.en: Since its primary [function] is not to come for atonement: for one does not bring it for a sin.

notes.he: דעולה מכפרת על עשה כדאמרינן במס' יומא (דף לו.) על עולה מתוודה עון שכחה ופאה:
notes.en: Since it atones for a positive [mitzva]: for a burnt offering atones for a positive mitzva, as we say in tractate Yoma (36a): over a burnt offering one confesses the sin of [neglecting] gleanings, forgotten sheaves and pe’a.

notes.he: כיון דמכפרא אעשה דאמרינן דבאה על עשה ועל לא תעשה שניתק (על) לעשה:
notes.en: Or perhaps: since it atones for a positive mitzva, for we say that it comes for a positive mitzva and for a prohibition that is rectified by a positive mitzva.

messages.text: Come and hear a resolution from a baraita:
With regard to one who plucks the wool from an unblemished firstborn, even though it later developed a blemish and the owner then slaughtered it, use of the wool is prohibited.

The reason use of the wool is prohibited is because he plucks it. But if it was torn out not by human intervention it is permitted. And this is correct all the more so with regard to a burnt offering, where one does not keep the animal any longer than necessary.
messages.quote: one who plucks the wool from an unblemished firstborn

messages.text: Actually, the same is true even if the wool of an unblemished firstborn animal was torn out by some other means; it is also prohibited.
messages.quote: But if it was torn out not by human intervention it is permitted

messages.text: And the reason that the baraita teaches the halakha using the term: One who plucks, is to convey to you the far-reaching nature of the opinion of Akavya ben Mahalalel, as he maintains that in the case of a blemished animal, discussed in the latter clause of the baraita, even if one plucks the wool it is permitted. Since the latter clause discusses a case where one plucked the wool himself, it is inferred that the former clause discusses the same situation.

notes.he: ולא בתם:
notes.en: For with a blemished one even plucking is permitted: but not with an unblemished one.

messages.text: But didn’t we learn in the mishna that the hair was shed rather than plucked?
messages.quote: even if one plucks the wool it is permitted

notes.he: אלמא בנשר שרי עקביא ולא בתלושין:
notes.en: But didn’t we learn “shed”: evidently Akavya permits [wool] that shed, and not [wool] that was plucked.

notes.he: בבעל מום ולא תולש:
notes.en: But didn’t we learn “shed”: with a blemished one, and not “plucks.”

messages.text: The mishna taught a case where the hair of the blemished animal was shed in order to convey to you the far-reaching nature of the opinion of the Rabbis, who deem the wool prohibited even in such a case.
messages.quote: the hair was shed rather than plucked

notes.he: דאפילו נשר דממילא אסרי אבל לעולם ה"ה לעקביא דתולש נמי מתיר:
notes.en: It taught “shed” to convey the far-reaching nature of the Rabbis: that they prohibit even [wool] that shed by itself; but in truth, the same is true for Akavya, that he permits even plucking.

messages.text: Conversely, the baraita taught a case where one plucks the hair in order to convey to you the far-reaching nature of the opinion of Akavya.

notes.he: דמתיר בשחיטה:
notes.en: It taught “plucks” to convey the far-reaching nature of Akavya: who permits [it] with slaughter.

messages.text: What is considered: That which does not appear to be part of the fleece?
messages.lead: § The mishna teaches that it is permitted to derive benefit from wool that is dangling from a firstborn but was not completely shed if it appears to be part of the fleece when the animal is shorn after death, but otherwise it is prohibited.
messages.quote: that which does not appear to be part of the fleece is prohibited

messages.text: This includes any strand of wool whose root is overturned and is facing toward the top, i.e., outward.
messages.quote: That which does not appear to be part of the fleece

notes.he: שכפול באמצעיתו ושני ראשין נראין בחוץ:
notes.en: Whose root is turned toward its head: that is folded in its middle, so that its two ends are seen outside.

notes.he: תולש והפוך העיקר כלפי ראשו וראשו אצל העור נראה שמחיים נתלש:
notes.en: Any whose root: of the hair is plucked, and the root is turned toward its head and its head is near the skin: it appears that it was plucked during [the animal’s] life.

messages.text: This includes any strand of wool that is not compressed together with the rest of the fleece, i.e., it sticks out when the fleece is pressed down.
messages.quote: That which does not appear to be part of the fleece

notes.he: שאינו שוה עם הגיזה אלא נראה עולה למעלה:
notes.en: That is not compressed: that is not level with the fleece but is seen rising upward.

notes.he: שאינו מתמעך עם הגיזה כלומר שאינו מחובר שוכב בשוה עם שאר הגיזה אלא נתלש ויוצא כמעט חוץ משאר הגיזה:
notes.en: That is not compressed with the fleece: that is, it is not attached, lying level with the rest of the fleece, but is plucked and sticks out almost outside the rest of the fleece.

messages.text: And what is the reason Reish Lakish did not state his explanation in accordance with the opinion of Rav Natan bar Oshaya, whose explanation is the more straightforward meaning of the phrase: That which does not appear to be part of the fleece?
messages.quote: any strand of wool that is not compressed together with the rest of the fleece

notes.dh: מאי טעמא לא אמר כרב נתן
notes.he: הא ודאי כיון דאינו מתמעך אינו נראה עם הגיזה קרינא ביה:
notes.en: What is the reason he did not state in accordance with Rav Natan: for certainly, since it is not compressed, “does not appear with the fleece” applies to it.

messages.text: Reish Lakish holds that the Sages did not deem strands of wool that are not compressed together with the rest of the fleece prohibited, because it is impossible for there to be fleece without dangling hairs. If Rav Natan bar Oshaya’s explanation were accepted, it would never be permitted to use such fleece of a dead firstborn animal. Consequently, Reish Lakish explains the statement of the mishna in a more lenient manner.
messages.quote: what is the reason Reish Lakish did not state his explanation in accordance with the opinion of Rav Natan bar Oshaya

notes.dh: לפי שאי אפשר לשום גיזה בלא נימין המדולדלות
notes.he: שעולות למעלה ואי כי האי גוונא מיתסר אין לך גיזה מותרת. רבי נתן טפי מחמיר להכי לא בעי מאי טעמא לא אמר כריש לקיש:
notes.en: Because it is impossible for any fleece to be without dangling hairs: that rise upward, and if in such a case it were prohibited, you would have no permitted fleece. Rabbi Natan [the daf: Rav Natan bar Oshaya] is the more stringent; that is why [the Gemara] does not ask, “What is the reason he did not state in accordance with Reish Lakish?”

notes.he: האי נמי שעיקרו הפוך כלפי ראשו ואינו יוצא חוץ משאר הגיזה היינו נראה עם הגיזה. קסבר ריש לקיש שעיקרו הפוך הוי ודאי אינו נראה עם הגיזה יותר ממה שאינו מתמעך דהכי אורחא דגיזה לפי שאי אפשר לגיזה בלא נימין המדולדלות:
notes.en: He holds: this too, whose root is turned toward its head but does not stick out beyond the rest of the fleece, is “appearing with the fleece.” Reish Lakish holds that [hair] whose root is turned certainly does not appear with the fleece, more than that which is not compressed, for that is the way of fleece, since it is impossible for fleece to be without dangling hairs.

notes.he: הדרן עלך הלוקח בהמה
notes.en: We will return to you, HaLoke’aḥ Behema [the end of chapter 3].

notes.he: הדרן עלך הלוקח
notes.en: We will return to you, HaLoke’aḥ [Behema].

messages.text: הדרן עלך הלוקח בהמה · Hadran alakh HaLoke’aḥ Behema: we will return to you, chapter 3, “One Who Purchases an Animal.”
Chapter 4 · עד כמה · Ad Kama: how long an Israelite must tend to a firstborn before giving it to the priest, and how long a firstborn may be kept.
Mishna

Until when must an Israelite tend to and raise a firstborn animal before giving it to the priest? With regard to a small animal, e.g., a sheep or goat, it is thirty days, and with regard to a large animal, e.g., cattle, it is fifty days.

notes.he: בזמן הזה קודם שיתננו לכהן שמוזהר לעכבו אצלו בעל כרחו ולפרנסו:
notes.en: Mishna. Until when [must an Israelite] tend to the firstborn: nowadays, before he gives it to the priest, for he is obliged to keep it with him whether he wishes or not, and to feed it.

notes.he: כי הך פלוגתא איכא לענין טיפול אבדה (ב"מ דף כח):
notes.en: Mishna. With a small animal, thirty days: there is a dispute like this one concerning tending a lost item (Bava Metzia 28).

notes.he: כלומר עד כמה ישראל חייב לגדל את הבכור קודם שיתנהו לכהן:
notes.en: Israelites are obligated to tend to the firstborn: that is, until when is an Israelite obligated to raise the firstborn before he gives it to the priest.

notes.dh: בדקה ל' יום ובגסה נ' יום
notes.he: כדמפרש בגמ':
notes.en: With a small animal, thirty days, and with a large one, fifty days: as is explained in the Gemara.

messages.text: With regard to a small animal, it is three months.
If the priest said to the owner within that period: Give it to me, that owner may not give it to him.

notes.he: בגמ' מפרש:
notes.en: He may not give it: it is explained in the Gemara.

notes.dh: אמר לו הכהן בתוך זה הזמן תנהו לי הרי זה לא יתן
notes.he: דנראה ככהן המסייע בבית הגרנות דאין נותנין לו תרומה דנראה כאלו נתנה לו בשכירותו אף כאן נמי נראה כאילו נותנו לו בשביל אותה הנאה שנכנס במקומו בטיפולו:
notes.en: If the priest said to him within that period, “Give it to me,” he may not give it: for he appears like a priest who assists at the threshing floors, to whom one may not give teruma, since it appears as if it was given to him as his wages. Here too it appears as if he gives it to him for that benefit, that he took his place in tending it.

messages.text: And if it is a blemished firstborn and the priest said to him: Give it to me so I may eat it, it is permitted for the owner to give it to him.

notes.dh: אם היה בעל מום ואומר לו
notes.he: הכהן בתוך הזמן תנהו לי שאוכלנו מותר:
notes.en: If it was blemished and he said to him: [that is,] the priest [said] within that period, “Give it to me so I may eat it,” it is permitted.

notes.he: ואם אמר לו בתוך הזמן כשנפל בו מום תן לי שאוכלנו מיד מותר הואיל ואין (רוצה) [צריך] הכהן לקיימו לא נראה כמסייע אבל בסתם הוא לא יתננו לו שאינו יכול לאוכלו מיד עד שיפול בו מום שלא בזמן בהמ"ק:
notes.en: And if, within the period, when a blemish developed in it, he said to him, “Give it to me so I may eat it” at once, it is permitted: since the priest does not need to keep it, he does not appear like one who assists. But in an ordinary case he may not give it to him, for he cannot eat it at once, until a blemish develops in it, when the Temple is not standing.

messages.text: And at the time that the Temple is standing, if it is unblemished and the priest said to him: Give it to me and I will sacrifice it, it is permitted for the owner to give it to him.

The firstborn animal is eaten year by year, i.e., within its first year, whether it is blemished or whether it is unblemished, as it is stated: “You shall eat it before the Lord your God year by year” (Deuteronomy 15:20).

verse.he: לִפְנֵי יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ תֹאכְלֶנּוּ שָׁנָה בְשָׁנָה בַּמָּקוֹם אֲשֶׁר־יִבְחַר יְהֹוָה אַתָּה וּבֵיתֶךָ׃
verse.en: You and your household shall eat it annually before the ETERNAL your God in the place that GOD will choose.

notes.he: בזמן שבית המקדש קיים:
notes.en: Whether unblemished: when the Temple is standing.

notes.he: בזמן הזה:
notes.en: Whether blemished: nowadays.

messages.text: If a blemish developed within its first year, it is permitted for the owner to maintain the animal for the entire twelve months. If a blemish developed after twelve months have passed, it is permitted for the owner to maintain the animal for only thirty days.
Gemara
From where are these matters derived?
messages.quote: it is thirty days, and with regard to a large animal, e.g., cattle, it is fifty days

notes.he: דל' יום חייב ליטפל בו:
notes.en: From where are these matters derived: that he is obligated to tend to it for thirty days.

messages.text: They are derived from a verse, as the verse states: “You shall not delay to offer of the fullness of your harvest, and of the outflow of your presses; you shall give to Me your firstborn sons. So you shall do with your oxen, and with your sheep; seven days it shall be with its mother, on the eighth day you shall give it to Me” (Exodus 22:28–29).
messages.quote: From where are these matters derived

verse.he: מְלֵאָתְךָ וְדִמְעֲךָ לֹא תְאַחֵר בְּכוֹר בָּנֶיךָ תִּתֶּן־לִי׃ כֵּן־תַּעֲשֶׂה לְשֹׁרְךָ לְצֹאנֶךָ שִׁבְעַת יָמִים יִהְיֶה עִם־אִמּוֹ בַּיּוֹם הַשְּׁמִינִי תִּתְּנוֹ־לִי׃
verse.en: You shall not put off the skimming of the first yield of your vats. You shall give Me the male first-born among your children. You shall do the same with your cattle and your flocks: seven days their male first-born shall remain with its mother; on the eighth day you shall give it to Me.

messages.text: The second part of verse 28 is juxtaposed to the second animal mentioned in verse 29. This juxtaposition teaches that just as a firstborn son is redeemed when he is thirty days old (Numbers 18:16), so too a sheep is given to the priest only when it is thirty days old.

The verses also state: “You shall not delay the fullness of your harvest, and of the outflow of your presses…So you shall do with your oxen” (Exodus 22:28–29). Just as the first fruits are brought on the festival of Shavuot, fifty days after Passover, so too the firstborn oxen are given to a priest when they are fifty days old.

notes.he: וסמיך ליה וכן תעשה לשורך לצאנך וגו' ודרשינן הכי בכור בניך תתן לי וכן לצאנך דכי היכי דבכור בניך מצותו לאחר שלשים כדכתיב (במדבר י״ח:ט״ו-ט״ז) ופדויו מבן חדש תפדה אף בכור צאן לאחר שלשים. מלאתך ודמעך דהיינו בכורים כן לשורך דכי היכי דבכורים לאחר חמשים שהרי בפסח התבואה מתבשלת ואין מביאין בכורים עד שיביאו שתי הלחם בעצרת כדאמרינן בפרק רבי ישמעאל (מנחות סח:):
notes.en: Gemara. “The fullness of your harvest and the outflow of your presses” etc.: and next to it, “So you shall do with your oxen, with your sheep” etc. We interpret it thus: “The firstborn of your sons you shall give to Me,” and so “with your sheep”: just as the mitzva of the firstborn of your sons is after thirty [days], as it is written: “And those that are to be redeemed of them, from a month old you shall redeem” (Numbers 18:15–16), so too the firstborn of the flock, after thirty. “The fullness of your harvest and the outflow of your presses,” that is, first fruits; so too “with your oxen”: just as first fruits are after fifty [days], for the grain ripens at Passover and first fruits are not brought until the two loaves are brought at Atzeret [Shavuot], as we say in the chapter Rabbi Yishmael (Menaḥot 68b).

notes.dh: מלאתך ודמעך לא תאחר כן תעשה לשורך
notes.he: דהיינו נ' ימים מיום הבאת העומר בפסח שגמר זמן בישול התבואה עד העצרת שמביאין שתי הלחם להתיר חדש במקדש וא"ת האי ביום חמשים הוא ולא הוי כעין בכור בניך וצאנך תתן לי דלאחר שלשים:
notes.en: “You shall not delay the fullness of your harvest and the outflow of your presses…so you shall do with your oxen”: that is, fifty days, from the day the omer is brought on Passover, which completes the ripening of the grain, until Atzeret, when the two loaves are brought to permit the new grain in the Temple. And if you say: this is on the fiftieth day, and it is not like “the firstborn of your sons… [so you shall do with] your sheep,” which is after thirty [days]. [The printed text gives no answer.]

notes.dh: דאמר קרא בכור בניך תתן לי וכתיב בבניך מבן חדש תפדה וכן תעשה לצאנך נמי
notes.he: מלאתך ודמעך לא תאחר וגרסי' במכילתא מלאתך אלו הבכורים שנוטלין מן המלא. ודמעך זו תרומה ומטמת גדוליה. למ"ה. ובכורים ואנן דמביא וקורא היינו מפסח ועד עצרת דאיכא נ' יום וכן תעשה לשורך היטפל בו נ' יום:
notes.en: For the verse states: “The firstborn of your sons you shall give to Me,” and of your sons it is written: “From a month old you shall redeem” (Numbers 18:16); “so you shall do with your sheep” as well. “You shall not delay the fullness of your harvest and your outflow”: and we read in the Mekhilta: “Your fullness” — these are the first fruits, which are taken from the full [crop]; “and your outflow” — this is teruma. (A footnote in the printed text suggests: “this is teruma, which renders the grain a mixture [meduma]”, in the words of “my teacher the Gaon.”) And with first fruits we hold that one brings and recites… (The printed text here is garbled.) …that one brings and recites, that is, from Passover until Atzeret, which is fifty days; “so you shall do with your oxen”: tend to it fifty days.

messages.text: Here, the first part of verse 28 is juxtaposed with the first animal mentioned in verse 29.
If these verses are the source, one can reverse the cases and derive that a firstborn ox must be given to the priest after thirty days, and a firstborn sheep after fifty days.

notes.he: דאימא בכור בניך תתן לי כן תעשה לשורך:
notes.en: Reverse it: let me say, “The firstborn of your sons you shall give to Me… so you shall do with your oxen.”

messages.text: It stands to reason that the time period that is alluded to earlier in the first verse corresponds to the animal that is mentioned earlier in the second verse, while the time period that is alluded to later in the first verse corresponds to the animal that is mentioned later in the second verse.

notes.he: מלאתך ודמעך קודמין בפסוק ראשון הלכך דרשינן להו אשורך הקודם בפסוק שני:
notes.en: The earlier to the earlier: “the fullness of your harvest and the outflow of your presses” come first in the first verse; therefore we apply them to “your oxen,” which comes first in the second verse.

notes.he: בכור בניך דמאחר בפסוק ראשון דרשינן ליה אצאנך המאוחר בפסוק שני:
notes.en: And the later: “the firstborn of your sons,” which comes later in the first verse, we apply to “your sheep,” which comes later in the second verse.

notes.he: מלאתך דמוקדם לפסוק הקיש לשורך שמוקדם לצאנך. ובכור בניך דמאחר אחר מלאתך תן לצאנך דמאוחר (אחר) לשורך:
notes.en: It stands to reason, the earlier to the earlier: “your fullness,” which is earlier in the verse, is juxtaposed with “your oxen,” which is earlier than “your sheep”; and “the firstborn of your sons,” which comes after “your fullness,” with “your sheep,” which comes after “your oxen.”

messages.text: On the contrary, it stands to reason that the time period that is alluded to closer to the mention of an animal should correspond to the animal, i.e., oxen, that is closest to it.

notes.he: ובכור בניך סמיך אל שורך:
notes.en: The adjacent to the adjacent: and “the firstborn of your sons” is adjacent to “your oxen.”

notes.he: בכור בניך סמיך לשורך:
notes.en: The adjacent to the adjacent: “the firstborn of your sons” is adjacent to “your oxen.”

messages.text: The halakha of both a firstborn sheep and a firstborn ox are juxtaposed with the halakha of a firstborn child, which teaches that both require at least thirty days. But since the verse states: “So you shall do with your oxen” (Exodus 22:29), the verse adds an extra act of doing for you in the case of your oxen.

verse.he: כֵּן־תַּעֲשֶׂה לְשֹׁרְךָ לְצֹאנֶךָ שִׁבְעַת יָמִים יִהְיֶה עִם־אִמּוֹ בַּיּוֹם הַשְּׁמִינִי תִּתְּנוֹ־לִי׃
verse.en: You shall do the same with your cattle and your flocks: seven days their male first-born shall remain with its mother; on the eighth day you shall give it to Me.

notes.he: דההוא תעשה לא צריך כלל אלא להוסיף עשייה בשורך יותר מצאנך:
notes.en: The verse states, “[so] you shall do with your oxen”: that “you shall do” is not needed at all, except to add [an extra] doing for your oxen beyond your sheep.

messages.text: In other words, the verse requires that the owner take care of an ox for additional time before giving it to the priest.
But if so, one can say that the owner must care for the ox an additional thirty days, making a total of sixty days. From where is the total of fifty days derived?
messages.quote: the verse adds an extra act of doing for you in the case of your oxen

notes.he: דעשייה אחרת דומיא דהך בכור בניך בעינן:
notes.en: And say sixty: for we require another “doing” like this one of “the firstborn of your sons.”

notes.he: הואיל דהוסיף לימא פי שנים מצאנך דהיינו שיתין:
notes.en: And say sixty: since it added, let it say twice [the time] of your sheep, that is, sixty.

messages.text: The interpretation of the verse with regard to the exact amount of time was given only to the Sages, and they determined that the owner must take care of his ox for fifty days.
messages.quote: making a total of sixty days

notes.he: הואיל ולא גילה לך שיעור עשייה שתוסיף ודאי לחכמים מסרך שיפרשו לך הטעם ואחריהם תלך:
notes.en: The verse gave it over only to the Sages: since it did not reveal to you the measure of the doing you should add, it certainly gave it over to the Sages to explain the reasoning to you, and you shall follow them.

notes.he: כלומר דלא אמר שיתין כפלים שבצאן אלא חכמים הוא דמפרשי נ' יום וסמכו אמלאתך ודמעך לא תאחר:
notes.en: The verse gave it over only to the Sages: that is, it did not say sixty, double [the time] for sheep; rather it is the Sages who explain fifty days, and they relied on “you shall not delay the fullness of your harvest and your outflow.”

messages.text: This is also taught in a baraita:

“You shall not delay to offer of the fullness of your harvest, and of the outflow of your presses; you shall give to Me your firstborn sons. So you shall do with your oxen, and with your sheep; seven days it shall be with its mother; on the eighth day you shall give it to Me” (Exodus 22:28–29).

One might have thought that this time period, i.e., thirty days, applies also to your oxen. Therefore, the verse states: “You shall do.” The verse adds an extra act of doing for you in the case of your oxen, and the interpretation of the verse was given only to the Sages.

From here the Sages stated: Until when must an Israelite tend to and raise a firstborn animal before handing it to the priest? With regard to a small animal, e.g., a sheep or goat, it is thirty days, and with regard to a large animal, e.g., cattle, it is fifty days.
With regard to a small animal, it is three months, because its tending is extensive, i.e., a great deal of work and effort are required in order to raise it before it can be given to a priest.

notes.he: טרחתה:
notes.en: Its tending: its trouble.

messages.text: So much effort is required to raise a sheep because its teeth are small and it cannot eat most foods.

notes.he: ואינה יכולה לאכול עשב ואם לא תהא עם האם תמות:
notes.en: Because its teeth are small: and it cannot eat grass, and if it is not with its mother it will die.

notes.he: ולא יכולה (ליכל) [למיכל] יפה עד ג' חדשים:
notes.en: Because its teeth are small: and it cannot eat well until three months.

messages.text: What is the reason?
messages.lead: § The mishna teaches: If the priest said to the owner within that period: Give it to me, that owner may not give it to him.
messages.quote: the priest said to the owner within that period: Give it to me, that owner may not give it to him

messages.text: Because such a priest appears like a priest who assists at the threshing floor so that he can be given teruma. Since this arrangement benefits the owner of the firstborn, as he is spared the effort of taking care of the animal throughout this period, it is as though this priest has paid for the right to receive the firstborn, which is prohibited.

notes.he: לפי שבזמן הזה אין בכור ראוי לכלום עד שיפול בו מום וכיון דעל ישראל רמיא ליטפל בו חמשים יום ואמר ליה הכהן בתוך הזמן תנהו לי ואזוננו ואף על פי שלא אהנה דומה כמי ששוכרו ומצילו מן הטורח ובלבד שיתננו לו ולא לכהן אחר ודומה לכהן שמסייע בבית הגרנות לדוש ולזרות כדי שיתנו לו התרומות. אבל אם היה בעל מום ואמר תן לי שאוכלנו הואיל וחזי ליה לא הוי ככהן המסייע:
notes.en: Because he appears like a priest who assists at the threshing floors: for nowadays a firstborn is not fit for anything until a blemish develops in it; and since it falls on the Israelite to tend to it for fifty days, if the priest said to him within that period, “Give it to me and I will feed it,” then even though he gave him no [real] benefit, he is like one who hires him and saves him the trouble, on condition that he gives it to him and not to another priest. So he is like a priest who assists at the threshing floors, threshing and winnowing so that they will give him the terumot. But if it was blemished and he said, “Give it to me so I may eat it,” since it is fit for him, he is not like a priest who assists.

messages.text: With regard to the priests, the Levites, and the poor people who assist in the home of the shepherd, or at the threshing floor, or in the slaughterhouse, one may not give them teruma or tithe as their wages.

notes.he: אכהנים קאי כדי ליתן להם הבכורות:
notes.en: In the home of the shepherds: refers to the priests, so that [the owners] will give them the firstborn animals.

notes.he: אכולהו קאי כהנים מפני תרומות ולוים משום מעשר ראשון ועניים משום מעשר עני:
notes.en: At the threshing floors: refers to all of them: the priests on account of teruma, the Levites on account of the first tithe, and the poor on account of the tithe for the poor.

notes.he: אכהנים קאי משום זרוע לחיים וקיבה:
notes.en: In the slaughterhouse: refers to the priests, on account of the foreleg, the jaw and the maw.

notes.he: לשמור או להאכיל כדי שיתנו להם הבכורות ולויים ועניים [המסייעים] בבית הגרנות מפני מעשר ראשון ומעשר עני והכהנים המסייעים בבית המטבחיים בשביל המתנות:
notes.en: The priests who assist in the home of the shepherds: to guard or to feed [the flock], so that they will give them the firstborn animals; and Levites and poor people [who assist] at the threshing floors, on account of the first tithe and the tithe for the poor; and the priests who assist in the slaughterhouse, for the sake of the gifts.

messages.text: And if one did so, he desecrated the sanctity of the item.

notes.he: שנתנו להן בשכרן:
notes.en: And if they did so: that they gave [these] to them as their wages.

notes.he: הוציאו התרומה והמעשר לחולין שאין בהן דין קדושה ולא יפה עשו ולא יצאו חובתן ויש בדבר עון מיתה:
notes.en: They desecrated: they turned the teruma and the tithe into non-sacred produce that has no law of sanctity; they did not act well and did not fulfill their obligation, and there is a sin [punishable by] death in the matter.

messages.text: And with regard to them the verse states: “But you are turned aside out of the way; you have caused many to stumble in the law; you have corrupted the covenant of Levi, says the Lord of hosts” (Malachi 2:8).

verse.he: וְאַתֶּם סַרְתֶּם מִן־הַדֶּרֶךְ הִכְשַׁלְתֶּם רַבִּים בַּתּוֹרָה שִׁחַתֶּם בְּרִית הַלֵּוִי אָמַר יְהֹוָה צְבָאוֹת׃
verse.en: But you have turned away from that course: You have made the many stumble through your rulings; you have corrupted the covenant of the Levites—said GOD of Hosts.

messages.text: And another verse states: “And you shall bear no sin by it, seeing that you have set apart the best from it; and you shall not desecrate the sacred items of the children of Israel, that you shall not die” (Numbers 18:32).

verse.he: וְלֹא־תִשְׂאוּ עָלָיו חֵטְא בַּהֲרִימְכֶם אֶת־חֶלְבּוֹ מִמֶּנּוּ וְאֶת־קׇדְשֵׁי בְנֵי־יִשְׂרָאֵל לֹא תְחַלְּלוּ וְלֹא תָמוּתוּ׃ {פ}
verse.en: You will incur no guilt through it, once you have removed the best part from it; but you must not profane the sacred donations of the Israelites, lest you die.

messages.text: What is the reason that the Gemara cites the second verse introduced with the phrase: And another verse states?
messages.quote: And another verse states

messages.text: And if you would say that the first verse indicates merely that teruma and tithe become desecrated, but one who does this is not punished by death, come and hear the second verse cited by the Gemara: “And you shall not desecrate the sacred items of the children of Israel, that you shall not die” (Numbers 18:32).

notes.dh: וכי תימא מיתה לא תלמוד לומר וכו'
notes.he: לאו דוקא דלא חשיב לה בפרק אלו הן הנשרפין (סנהדרין פג.) בהדי אלו שבמיתה אלא קרוב הוא [לעון] מיתה:
notes.en: And if you would say: not death, [come and hear] etc.: not precisely, for it is not counted in the chapter Elu Hen HaNisrafin (Sanhedrin 83a) among those [liable to] death [at the hand of Heaven]; rather, it is close to a sin [punishable by] death.

messages.text: And the Sages wished to penalize those who gave teruma or tithe to the priests, Levites, or poor people who helped them, and to require them to separate in their place complete teruma, so that the owners of the produce would not benefit from their improper actions.

notes.he: את הבעלי בתים:
notes.en: To penalize them: the householders.

notes.he: תרומה ומעשרות פעם שניה משלם:
notes.en: [To separate] teruma and tithes a second time, in full.

messages.text: And for what reason did the Sages not penalize them? Perhaps they would mistakenly think that the produce has not yet been tithed at all, and they would come to separate teruma and tithes from it when it is actually exempt produce, as by Torah law it has already had its tithes removed. They might then separate teruma and tithes from it on behalf of produce to which the obligation of separating tithes still applies, i.e., regular untithed produce.

notes.he: דשמא יהו להם שני סאין אחד של טבל גמור ואחד הופרש ממנה לכהן המסייע ואי אמרת ליה דהדרא ולפרוש מינה משום קנסא סבר בעל הבית טבל גמור הוא ומפריש ממנה עלה דאידך ואיהי פטורה מדאורייתא אלא קנסא הוא:
notes.en: From the exempt for the obligated: for perhaps they will have two se’a, one fully untithed and one from which [teruma] was separated [and given] to the priest who assists. If you tell him that it reverts and he must separate [teruma] from it as a penalty, the householder will think it is fully untithed and will separate from it for the other one, though by Torah law it is exempt and [the second separation] is only a penalty.

notes.dh: דלמא אתי לאפרושי מן הפטור על החיוב כו'
notes.he: בכמה מקומות אמרינן תרומה ויחזור ויתרום ולא גזרינן התם כיון שהתרומה ראשונה לכהן מידע ידע דשניה דרבנן ואפילו נתן הראשונה כבר לכהן קודם שיאמר לו חכם לחזור ולתרום מ"מ מדאין הכהן מחזיר לו את הראשונה מידע ידע דשניה דרבנן היא אבל כאן סבור הוא שנתן לכהן בתורת שכר סיועו ומעכבה כהן ובכמה מקומות צריך לחלק בדברים כי ההיא דפסחים בריש מקום שנהגו (פסחים דף נא.) גבי הנהו דמפרשו חלתא מארוזא דאמרינן דאי רובא לאו אורז אכלי ניכלה זר באנפייהו דלמא אתו לאפרושי מן הפטור על החיוב ובפ"ק דיומא (דף י.) גבי סוכת החג בחג חייבת [בעירוב] ובמזוזה ובמעשר דקאמר התם דמדאורייתא קאמר דאי מדרבנן דלמא אתא לאפרושי מן הפטור על החיוב ובדמאי הלוקח מן עובד כוכבים למ"ד יש קנין חייבו חכמים ולא חשו לכך:
notes.en: Perhaps he will come to separate from the exempt for the obligated etc.: In several places we say, “[It is] teruma, and he must separate teruma again,” and there we do not make this decree, because the first teruma goes to the priest, so he knows that the second is rabbinic. And even if he had already given the first to the priest before a Sage told him to separate again, nevertheless, since the priest does not return the first to him, he knows that the second is rabbinic. But here he thinks he gave it to the priest as wages for his help, and [so] the priest keeps it. And in several places one must draw distinctions in such matters, such as in Pesaḥim at the beginning of Makom SheNahagu (Pesaḥim 51a), about those who separated ḥalla from rice, where we said that if most people do not eat rice, a non-priest should eat it in front of them, lest they come to separate from the exempt for the obligated; and in the first chapter of Yoma (10a), about the sukka of the festival being obligated, on the festival, in eruv, mezuza and tithe, where it says there that it speaks by Torah law, for if [the obligation were] rabbinic, perhaps one would come to separate from the exempt for the obligated; and with demai, one who buys from a gentile, according to the one who holds that [a gentile] has ownership [in the Land of Israel], the Sages obligated him [to tithe] and were not concerned about this.

notes.he: אלא משום דדלמא אתי לאפרושי מן הפטור על החיוב דאי מחייבינן ליה לאפרושי תרומה אחריתי סבר הך גברא כולי הך תבואה טבל ודאי כאילו לא נתרמה כלל ואי אית ליה טבל אחריתי דודאי טבל אתו לאפרושי עליה מהך תבואה שכבר נתן ממנה והיא כבר נפטרה (דסבר דלאו משום קנסא הוא דקנסינן ליה לאפרושי תרומה אחריתי אלא משום חיוב גמור) ואתי לאפרושי מן הפטור על החיוב ולהכי לא קנסינן ליה:
notes.en: Rather, because perhaps he would come to separate from the exempt for the obligated: for if we obligated him to separate another teruma, this man would think that all this grain is definitely untithed, as if no teruma had been separated from it at all. And if he has other produce that is definitely untithed, he would come to separate for it from this grain, from which he already gave and which was already exempted (for he would think that we required him to separate another teruma not as a penalty but as a full obligation), and so he would come to separate from the exempt for the obligated. Therefore we do not penalize him.

messages.text: And in all of these cases, although it is prohibited to give the teruma and tithe to a priest or Levite as his wages, nevertheless there is…
Continued on 27a: …the benefit of discretion for the owners, that is, the right to choose which priest or Levite receives their gifts.
